claims.text: The brief's three load-bearing artifacts describe one trip and one trip only: TRP-00529 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown alike, and the trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100% coverage, a 10-second sampling interval, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. The rider's initial showing on identity under POL-RD-08 is therefore made, and it is made on evidence that no impairment discounts — this is not a case where the trace itself is in question under POL-RD-07.

The rider does not ask the tribunal to call 110 metres a deviation, because the record forbids it. The governing figure is the trace distance of 2.61 km against a booked optimal of 2.5 km — an excess of 0.11 km, or 4.4% — which fails both POL-RD-01 gates, the 0.8 km absolute gate and the 20% gate, so no distance deviation is established on this trip and no distance recomputation follows on that line. The rider's money is not in the 110 metres; it is in the time and waiting lines the fare actually turns on.

The delay the rider is charged for has no record behind it. The only account anyone offers for the extra time is the driver's 'meter waiting time is part of the fare ... taxis charge for jams', and under POL-RD-13 an external traffic cause is tested against this trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. The bundle's only advisory is MISSING: EV-ADVIS-00529-01 carries no payload, weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the comparison cannot be run, the jam explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and no adjusted optimal or excused distance can follow from it. Please note I am relying on that artifact with its impairment disclosed: it is absent, not clean. What remains on the record is 24.0 metered minutes against a 9.0-minute optimal route on a vehicle that covered essentially the optimal distance.

Nothing in the record reconciles the charge the rider is made to carry. The fare does add up to charged_total of SGD 16.35 (3.80 base + 1.95 distance + 6.72 time + 3.08 waiting + 0.80 platform), but the contested SGD 5.40 corresponds to no line, no rate and no recorded fact: the 15 metered minutes above the 9-minute optimal have no advisory to explain them (EV-ADVIS-00529-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0), and the 3.08 waiting line stands against a recorded wait_time_min of 1.0 with no waiting-time rate anywhere in the record. A deciding fact carried solely by an artifact at a weight below the 0.70 floor cannot ground a ruling under POL-GEN-02, and where that is so POL-RD-10 requires escalation rather than a final ruling. Escalation holds the disputed SGD 5.40 instead of collecting it, whereas a NO_ACTION on this rider-filed dispute would leave the rider carrying the charge (POL-GEN-03).

The rider's own profile does not trigger the enhanced corroboration gate in POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so this claim does not require corroboration beyond the trace and the rider is not to be treated as a serial filer. That does not create a deviation, but it means the rider's account of this trip is not to be discounted, and the tracker fields on that profile are cited only for the test POL-RD-08 names.

claims.text: The route-deviation threshold in POL-RD-01 is not met on this trip's own trace, and the GPS artifact says so in terms: the derived deviation status is 'no deviation'. The measured excess is 0.11 km, or 4.400% of the 2.5 km optimal route, against gates of 0.8 km absolute and 20% that must BOTH be exceeded. POL-RD-01 provides that if either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The rider's case is therefore over at the first gate.

POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure to govern over the rounded convenience copy on the trip_record, and I take the trace figure as it directs: trace_distance_km 2.61 km against optimal_distance_km 2.5 km. The point is in any event immaterial to the outcome, because the excess is 0.11 km on the trace and roughly 0.1 km on the rounded actual_distance_km of 2.6 km - an order of magnitude below the 0.8 km gate and a fifth of the 20% gate on either reading. There is no reading of this record on which the deviation gate opens.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden, and limb (b) of that clause requires her to show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. She has not: the excess she must prove is 4.4% and 0.11 km, well under both gates. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver at all, and the driver is not called upon to point to any exculpatory artifact. No traffic_advisory is needed to answer a defence that consists entirely of a failed numeric test, and the driver's answering statement that metered waiting time forms part of the fare is an explanation, not an invocation of POL-RD-03.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 and I say so expressly so that the point cannot be run against the driver: 145 fixes at a 10 s cadence across a 24-minute trip, coverage_pct 100.0, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0 - no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds. None of limbs (a) to (c) is engaged, so the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route (impaired trace with no independent corroboration) is closed, and the excess figure may be relied on directly. The trace also identifies the same trip as the other artifacts: first_fix_at 18:31:40 matches trip_record.started_at, and last_fix_at 18:55:40 matches ended_at, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied and the POL-RD-10(4) timestamp-disagreement trigger does not fire.

The bundle's traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00529-01, has admissibility status MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, and I disclose that plainly: it carries no payload and can establish no fact; its only citable content is its own absence. That absence does not escalate this case. POL-RD-13(1) provides that where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and no party here invokes POL-RD-03 on the driver's side - the driver's answer is that the threshold was never crossed, not that traffic excused a crossing. POL-RD-10(5) is therefore not triggered by this artifact, and no exculpatory clause has been invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool.

POL-RD-02's recomputation runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'. No deviation is established, so the recomputation is never reached, no recomputed_fare arises and no refund is available on the distance or time lines. The congestion the rider describes is priced by the meter itself and is itemised on the fare breakdown under rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDETAXI: time_fare 6.72 and a waiting_time_fee of 3.08, against a total_charged of 16.35. Nothing in this policy makes metered time refundable in the absence of a deviation, and the rider's wider grievance - that the app was cheaper before electric vehicles - is not a ground any loaded clause provides for; I do not ask the tribunal to change the policy, only to apply it.

NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03: it means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands - fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd are left exactly as they are. This dispute is rider-filed, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so NO_ACTION leaves the SGD 16.35 metered fare standing in full and the driver retains it. The contested SGD 5.40 is not returned, and nothing is netted against the driver.

Even if the tribunal ran the POL-RD-06 check, no pattern could be established against this driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 250, and 0 divided by 250 is far below the 0.05 ratio that clause requires, while the count itself is below the threshold of 3. It follows that no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is open on this record. I rely on no other field of either profile: POL-GEN-01 confines rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate, prior_deviation_flags, prior_no_show_flags and the rest to context, and I cite none of them as a ground.

The driver's own track corroborates slow movement in traffic rather than any detour: across 145 fixes the distinct speeds run continuously between 4.6 and 8.2 km/h, and the entire 2.61 km trace exceeds the 2.5 km optimal route by only 0.11 km. A driver who had taken another road to avoid or exploit congestion would show excess distance; this trace shows almost none. The single 100-second in-app call the rider complains of is recorded on the trip record as placed by the driver at 19:35:40, after the trip ended at 18:55:40, and whatever its tone it is not a fact from which a metered fare becomes refundable under any clause of this policy.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: I have applied the Route Deviation policy to trip TRP-00529, and the fare stands. The rider's distance complaint fails at the very first gate, and with it the whole claim.

POL-RD-01 requires an excess distance greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% of the optimal route; both tests must pass. The governing figure is the GPS trace, and EV-GPS-00529 measures a trace distance of 2.61 km against the booked optimal of 2.5 km on EV-TRIP-00529 — an excess of 0.11 km, or 4.400%, against gates of 0.8 km and 20%. Neither gate is close, so no deviation is established and POL-RD-02's recomputation is never reached. The SGD 1.95 distance line and the SGD 6.72 time line are not refundable on that ground.

I tested the trace for impairment, as both sides asked. EV-GPS-00529 carries 145 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07's limbs (a) to (c) fires: the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. Identity also checks out — TRP-00529 appears on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace's first and last fixes (18:31:40 and 18:55:40) match the trip record's start and end — so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire.

The rider is right about one thing, and it changes nothing. The driver's 'taxis charge for jams' explanation has no traffic advisory behind it: the bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00529-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I name that artifact, its weight and its issue code as POL-GEN-02(3) requires. No advisory comparison can be run, and the jam explanation therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08. But an excuse that carries no weight cannot produce a refund where the measured excess never reaches the POL-RD-01 gate in the first place. The rider's congestion time is priced by the meter she took: the fare breakdown shows time_fare SGD 6.72 and waiting_time_fee SGD 3.08 inside a charged_total of SGD 16.35 (base fare 3.80, distance 1.95, platform fee 0.80). No loaded clause makes metered time refundable absent a deviation, and POL-RD-13's consequence (2) — deviation standing at the measured figure — cannot apply because the threshold was never shown. Nor is there an exculpatory clause for the driver to have invoked: the driver's answer is that the numeric test was never met, not that a closure excused a crossing. POL-RD-13(1) therefore applies, and the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation; nothing escalates this case.

On the driver's profile, the POL-RD-06 check comes out clean: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arise. I rely on no other profile field; POL-GEN-01 confines rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate and the like to context, and I have used none of them. The rider's own profile raises no enhanced-corroboration gate either (deviation_claims_60d is 0).

I have noted the driver's 100-second in-app call of 19:35:40, placed after the trip ended at 18:55:40. Whatever was said on it, it is not a fact that makes a metered fare refundable under any clause of this policy, and the rider's wider grievance that the app was cheaper before electric vehicles is not a ground the policy provides.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 this is party-relative — the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands. This is a rider-filed dispute with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the SGD 16.35 metered fare stands in full, the contested SGD 5.40 is not returned, and nothing is netted against the driver. My confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor, so no escalation follows.

The 24 metered minutes are the congestion time you are paying for; no clause in this policy makes metered time refundable absent a deviation, and your broader point about app pricing is not a ground any loaded clause provides.

Driver: your fare stands and nothing is netted against you. Your profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern — deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 250 completed trips in 90 days — so no POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. Two advocate claims that sought escalation on the missing advisory were removed at the mechanical check for citing an impaired artifact without naming its issue code (IMPAIRMENT_UNDISCLOSED); the escalation they proposed was, in any event, not supported by a POL-RD-10 trigger. Confidence is 0.90, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding facts (the GPS trace and trip record for the no-deviation finding, the fare breakdown for the charge lines); the MISSING advisory carries no fact and therefore does not cap confidence.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. This ruling is NO_ACTION: the fare of SGD 16.35 stands as charged (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) and the contested SGD 5.40 is not refunded.

The route-deviation tests, which this case is filed under, do not open. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00529, weight 1.0, 145 fixes at a 10 s cadence, coverage 100%, no gaps, max gap 0 s) measures the trip at 2.61 km against a booked optimal of 2.5 km — an excess of 0.11 km, or 4.4% of the optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds BOTH 0.8 km and 20% of the optimal route. It clears neither gate. POL-RD-01 says in terms that where either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised, and the trace figure governs over the rounded 2.6 km convenience copy on the trip record. Both advocates agree on this, and I agree with them.

Rider — what you are really disputing is the time spent in traffic and the waiting charge, not the distance. The trip is a metered fare: charged_total 16.35 = base 3.80 + distance 1.95 + time 6.72 (24.0 metered minutes at 0.28/min) + waiting 3.08 + platform fee 0.80, on rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDETAXI with fare_model METERED. POL-RD-02, which would recompute the fare against the optimal route, runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01'. None is, so that computation is never reached and no line of the fare is refundable. No clause makes metered time refundable because the optimal run is 9 minutes: a meter charges the time actually taken. Your wider point, that the app was cheaper before electric vehicles, is not a ground any loaded clause provides and I do not decide it.

Your reliance on the absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00529-01: status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) does not change that. The artifact is absent, so it can carry no fact and cannot found a refund; under POL-RD-13(1) a missing advisory that no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and it is not an escalation trigger here. I record that no traffic advisory covering the trip window was on file. It is also not the artifact carrying the deciding fact: that fact — an excess of 0.11 km and 4.4% — is carried by EV-GPS-00529 and EV-TRIP-00529, both at weight 1.0, so nothing caps confidence below the 0.70 floor and POL-RD-10(1) does not fire.

Driver — your account is consistent with the record. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (no gap over 90 s, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sampling interval above 30 s), so the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is closed. Trip identifiers and start/end timestamps match across the trip record and the trace (18:31:40 and 18:55:40), so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire. Your profile shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days over 250 trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06: no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is open, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. No unbilled-distance compensation arises under POL-RD-04 either — distance charged 2.6 km against a 2.61 km trace is a shortfall of 0.01 km, well under 1.0 km. The rider's profile (0 deviation claims in 60 days) does not trigger the POL-RD-08 enhanced-corroboration gate, but that does not create a deviation.

Two collateral points. First, the driver's in-app call to the rider at 19:35:40 falls after the trip ended at 18:55:40; it is a service matter rather than a fare item, no clause turns it into a refundable charge, and without an established repeat pattern it produces no conduct referral. Whether the platform wishes to look at it as customer service is for the platform. Second, the counterparty statement ('meter waiting time is part of the fare') is consistent with the metered model and adds nothing to the fare; the counterparty statement carries no weight multiplier and enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the confidence cap.

No referrals are recorded: on these facts no clause of the loaded policy produces one.

Confidence is 0.95. The finding rests on EV-GPS-00529 and EV-TRIP-00529, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, and no impaired artifact carries the deciding fact.

This ruling is NO_ACTION: the fare of SGD 16.35 stands as charged (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) and the contested SGD 5.40 is not refunded.

The route-deviation tests, which this case is filed under, do not open. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00529, weight 1.0, 145 fixes at a 10 s cadence, coverage 100%, no gaps, max gap 0 s) measures the trip at 2.61 km against a booked optimal of 2.5 km — an excess of 0.11 km, or 4.4% of the optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds BOTH 0.8 km and 20% of the optimal route. It clears neither gate. POL-RD-01 says in terms that where either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised, and the trace figure governs over the rounded 2.6 km convenience copy on the trip record. Both advocates agree on this, and I agree with them.

Rider — what you are really disputing is the time spent in traffic and the waiting charge, not the distance. The trip is a metered fare: charged_total 16.35 = base 3.80 + distance 1.95 + time 6.72 (24.0 metered minutes at 0.28/min) + waiting 3.08 + platform fee 0.80, on rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDETAXI with fare_model METERED. POL-RD-02, which would recompute the fare against the optimal route, runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01'. None is, so that computation is never reached and no line of the fare is refundable. No clause makes metered time refundable because the optimal run is 9 minutes: a meter charges the time actually taken. Your wider point, that the app was cheaper before electric vehicles, is not a ground any loaded clause provides and I do not decide it.

Your reliance on the absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00529-01: status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) does not change that. The artifact is absent, so it can carry no fact and cannot found a refund; under POL-RD-13(1) a missing advisory that no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and it is not an escalation trigger here. I record that no traffic advisory covering the trip window was on file. It is also not the artifact carrying the deciding fact: that fact — an excess of 0.11 km and 4.4% — is carried by EV-GPS-00529 and EV-TRIP-00529, both at weight 1.0, so nothing caps confidence below the 0.70 floor and POL-RD-10(1) does not fire.

Driver — your account is consistent with the record. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (no gap over 90 s, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sampling interval above 30 s), so the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is closed. Trip identifiers and start/end timestamps match across the trip record and the trace (18:31:40 and 18:55:40), so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire. Your profile shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days over 250 trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06: no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is open, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. No unbilled-distance compensation arises under POL-RD-04 either — distance charged 2.6 km against a 2.61 km trace is a shortfall of 0.01 km, well under 1.0 km. The rider's profile (0 deviation claims in 60 days) does not trigger the POL-RD-08 enhanced-corroboration gate, but that does not create a deviation.

Two collateral points. First, the driver's in-app call to the rider at 19:35:40 falls after the trip ended at 18:55:40; it is a service matter rather than a fare item, no clause turns it into a refundable charge, and without an established repeat pattern it produces no conduct referral. Whether the platform wishes to look at it as customer service is for the platform. Second, the counterparty statement ('meter waiting time is part of the fare') is consistent with the metered model and adds nothing to the fare; the counterparty statement carries no weight multiplier and enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the confidence cap.

No referrals are recorded: on these facts no clause of the loaded policy produces one.

Confidence is 0.95. The finding rests on EV-GPS-00529 and EV-TRIP-00529, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, and no impaired artifact carries the deciding fact."},"discarded_claims":[{"claim":"Nothing in the record reconciles the charge the rider is made to carry. ruling.explanation:
To both parties. This is a 2.6 km taxi trip, ION Orchard to Great World on 17 Sep 2026, charged at SGD 16.35 on rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDETAXI. The charge stands: the evidence does not support a refund, and both money fields are empty.

The distance test fails on the trip's own record. The governing figure is the GPS trace's 2.61 km against the booked optimal of 2.5 km (POL-RD-01), an excess of 0.11 km, or 4.4%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds both 0.8 km and 20% of the optimal route; this excess fails both gates, so no deviation exists on this trip and the distance field decides nothing. Rider advocate's own second claim concedes exactly this, and the driver's answer on the same point is accepted: the trace figure governs over the rounded 2.6 km convenience copy, and neither reading opens the gate.

The rider's real complaint is the time billed — 24.0 metered minutes against a 9.0-minute optimal route — and the SGD 3.08 waiting-time line, with the driver's explanation that 'meter waiting time is part of the fare'. The frustration is understandable, but no loaded clause makes metered time or waiting time refundable where no route deviation is established. The POL-RD-02 recomputation runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'; it is therefore never reached, and the SGD 12.075 recomputed figure and the SGD 4.30 it would imply are not payable. The SGD 16.35 is base 3.80 + distance 1.95 + time 6.72 + waiting 3.08 + platform fee 0.80, which is what the meter produced, and the fare breakdown's own derived arithmetic matches that total.

The driver's traffic explanation needs no advisory behind it, because the driver was never called on to excuse anything: the rider's own trace shows no deviation, so the POL-RD-08 burden never shifted to the driver, and an uncited assertion carries no weight in any event. For completeness, the bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00529-01, is status MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. I name it and its weight as POL-GEN-02(3) requires, and I confirm the finding does not rest on it: its absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it (POL-RD-13(1)), so it neither excuses the driver nor escalates the case, and the trace at weight 1.0 alone disposes of the dispute.

The trace is not impaired. It carries 145 fixes at a 10 s cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, max_gap_sec 0.0, no jump over 500 m and no sustained interval over 30 s, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) is not engaged and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is closed. The artifacts identify the same trip (TRP-00529 on all three; first_fix_at 18:31:40 matches trip_record.started_at, last_fix_at 18:55:40 matches ended_at), so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied and no POL-RD-10(4) timestamp trigger fires.

On the profiles: the driver's POL-RD-06 figures are deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established — no FULL_REFUND uplift under limb (b) and no conduct referral under limb (c). The rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no enhanced-corroboration gate under POL-RD-08 applies; that does not create a deviation either. No other profile field is used as a ground. Nothing shows a billing-integrity defect: no ERP gantry was charged (tolls 0.00, erp_gantries empty) and no airport surcharge was applied, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to correct and produces no referral. The driver's post-trip phone call is recorded (100 seconds, placed at 19:35:40, after the 18:55:40 end) and is not a fact any clause of this policy turns into a refund. The rider's wider point that the app was cheaper under an earlier fleet is a policy question, not a charge any loaded clause can unwind.

Because this is a rider-filed dispute, NO_ACTION leaves the fare as charged: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stand, and the contested SGD 5.40 is not returned. I have no doubt in this outcome and the escalation routes do not fire.

discards.claim: Nothing in the record reconciles the charge the rider is made to carry. The fare does add up to charged_total of SGD 16.35 (3.80 base + 1.95 distance + 6.72 time + 3.08 waiting + 0.80 platform), but the contested SGD 5.40 corresponds to no line, no rate and no recorded fact: the 15 metered minutes above the 9-minute optimal have no advisory to explain them (EV-ADVIS-00529-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0), and the 3.08 waiting line stands against a recorded wait_time_min of 1.0 with no waiting-time rate anywhere in the record. A deciding fact carried solely by an artifact at a weight below the 0.70 floor cannot ground a ruling under POL-GEN-02, and where that is so POL-RD-10 requires escalation rather than a final ruling. Escalation holds the disputed SGD 5.40 instead of collecting it, whereas a NO_ACTION on this rider-filed dispute would leave the rider carrying the charge (POL-GEN-03).

That absence does not escalate this case. POL-RD-13(1) provides that where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and no party here invokes POL-RD-03 on the driver's side - the driver's answer is that the threshold was never crossed, not that traffic excused a crossing. It follows that no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is open on this record. I rely on no other field of either profile: POL-GEN-01 confines rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate, prior_deviation_flags, prior_no_show_flags and the rest to context, and I cite none of them as a ground.

ledger.claim: The brief's three load-bearing artifacts describe one trip and one trip only: TRP-00529 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown alike, and the trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100% coverage, a 10-second sampling interval, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. The rider's initial showing on identity under POL-RD-08 is therefore made, and it is made on evidence that no impairment discounts — this is not a case where the trace itself is in question under POL-RD-07.

The rider does not ask the tribunal to call 110 metres a deviation, because the record forbids it. The governing figure is the trace distance of 2.61 km against a booked optimal of 2.5 km — an excess of 0.11 km, or 4.4% — which fails both POL-RD-01 gates, the 0.8 km absolute gate and the 20% gate, so no distance deviation is established on this trip and no distance recomputation follows on that line. The rider's money is not in the 110 metres; it is in the time and waiting lines the fare actually turns on.

The delay the rider is charged for has no record behind it. The only account anyone offers for the extra time is the driver's 'meter waiting time is part of the fare ... taxis charge for jams', and under POL-RD-13 an external traffic cause is tested against this trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. The bundle's only advisory is MISSING: EV-ADVIS-00529-01 carries no payload, weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the comparison cannot be run, the jam explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and no adjusted optimal or excused distance can follow from it. Please note I am relying on that artifact with its impairment disclosed: it is absent, not clean. What remains on the record is 24.0 metered minutes against a 9.0-minute optimal route on a vehicle that covered essentially the optimal distance.

Nothing in the record reconciles the charge the rider is made to carry. The fare does add up to charged_total of SGD 16.35 (3.80 base + 1.95 distance + 6.72 time + 3.08 waiting + 0.80 platform), but the contested SGD 5.40 corresponds to no line, no rate and no recorded fact: the 15 metered minutes above the 9-minute optimal have no advisory to explain them (EV-ADVIS-00529-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0), and the 3.08 waiting line stands against a recorded wait_time_min of 1.0 with no waiting-time rate anywhere in the record. A deciding fact carried solely by an artifact at a weight below the 0.70 floor cannot ground a ruling under POL-GEN-02, and where that is so POL-RD-10 requires escalation rather than a final ruling. Escalation holds the disputed SGD 5.40 instead of collecting it, whereas a NO_ACTION on this rider-filed dispute would leave the rider carrying the charge (POL-GEN-03).

ledger.claim: The rider's own profile does not trigger the enhanced corroboration gate in POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so this claim does not require corroboration beyond the trace and the rider is not to be treated as a serial filer. That does not create a deviation, but it means the rider's account of this trip is not to be discounted, and the tracker fields on that profile are cited only for the test POL-RD-08 names.

The route-deviation threshold in POL-RD-01 is not met on this trip's own trace, and the GPS artifact says so in terms: the derived deviation status is 'no deviation'. The measured excess is 0.11 km, or 4.400% of the 2.5 km optimal route, against gates of 0.8 km absolute and 20% that must BOTH be exceeded. POL-RD-01 provides that if either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The rider's case is therefore over at the first gate.

POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure to govern over the rounded convenience copy on the trip_record, and I take the trace figure as it directs: trace_distance_km 2.61 km against optimal_distance_km 2.5 km. The point is in any event immaterial to the outcome, because the excess is 0.11 km on the trace and roughly 0.1 km on the rounded actual_distance_km of 2.6 km - an order of magnitude below the 0.8 km gate and a fifth of the 20% gate on either reading. There is no reading of this record on which the deviation gate opens.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden, and limb (b) of that clause requires her to show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. She has not: the excess she must prove is 4.4% and 0.11 km, well under both gates. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver at all, and the driver is not called upon to point to any exculpatory artifact. No traffic_advisory is needed to answer a defence that consists entirely of a failed numeric test, and the driver's answering statement that metered waiting time forms part of the fare is an explanation, not an invocation of POL-RD-03.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 and I say so expressly so that the point cannot be run against the driver: 145 fixes at a 10 s cadence across a 24-minute trip, coverage_pct 100.0, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0 - no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds. None of limbs (a) to (c) is engaged, so the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route (impaired trace with no independent corroboration) is closed, and the excess figure may be relied on directly. The trace also identifies the same trip as the other artifacts: first_fix_at 18:31:40 matches trip_record.started_at, and last_fix_at 18:55:40 matches ended_at, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied and the POL-RD-10(4) timestamp-disagreement trigger does not fire.

The bundle's traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00529-01, has admissibility status MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, and I disclose that plainly: it carries no payload and can establish no fact; its only citable content is its own absence. That absence does not escalate this case. POL-RD-13(1) provides that where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and no party here invokes POL-RD-03 on the driver's side - the driver's answer is that the threshold was never crossed, not that traffic excused a crossing. POL-RD-10(5) is therefore not triggered by this artifact, and no exculpatory clause has been invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool.

ledger.claim: POL-RD-02's recomputation runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'. No deviation is established, so the recomputation is never reached, no recomputed_fare arises and no refund is available on the distance or time lines. The congestion the rider describes is priced by the meter itself and is itemised on the fare breakdown under rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDETAXI: time_fare 6.72 and a waiting_time_fee of 3.08, against a total_charged of 16.35. Nothing in this policy makes metered time refundable in the absence of a deviation, and the rider's wider grievance - that the app was cheaper before electric vehicles - is not a ground any loaded clause provides for; I do not ask the tribunal to change the policy, only to apply it.

NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03: it means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands - fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd are left exactly as they are. This dispute is rider-filed, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so NO_ACTION leaves the SGD 16.35 metered fare standing in full and the driver retains it. The contested SGD 5.40 is not returned, and nothing is netted against the driver.

Even if the tribunal ran the POL-RD-06 check, no pattern could be established against this driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 250, and 0 divided by 250 is far below the 0.05 ratio that clause requires, while the count itself is below the threshold of 3. It follows that no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is open on this record. I rely on no other field of either profile: POL-GEN-01 confines rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate, prior_deviation_flags, prior_no_show_flags and the rest to context, and I cite none of them as a ground.

ledger.claim: The driver's own track corroborates slow movement in traffic rather than any detour: across 145 fixes the distinct speeds run continuously between 4.6 and 8.2 km/h, and the entire 2.61 km trace exceeds the 2.5 km optimal route by only 0.11 km. A driver who had taken another road to avoid or exploit congestion would show excess distance; this trace shows almost none. The single 100-second in-app call the rider complains of is recorded on the trip record as placed by the driver at 19:35:40, after the trip ended at 18:55:40, and whatever its tone it is not a fact from which a metered fare becomes refundable under any clause of this policy.
